text:
Aria: Quick sync — I'm running a small experiment to reduce coldstarts without permanently keeping GPUs warm. idea: a lightweight keepalive heartbeat from a daemonset that annotates nodes with a short TTL so CA and our drain logic treat them as 'recently active' instead of permanent warm-pool members.

Jordan: hmm interesting. is this different from the existing warm-pool controller?

Aria: yes. warm-pool today is a separate nodepool with prewarmed images. problem: long tail of pods keeps nodes alive and we overprovision. heartbeat approach marks nodes for a soft grace period (eg 5m) after any inference activity. if no activity and TTL expires, normal downscale can evict.

Sam: can the autoscaler see that TTL? we don't want CA to ignore nodes forever.

Aria: plan is to use an annotation + Prom metric. CA uses node_utilization and taints. we won't change CA logic — instead our drain controller will skip nodes with annotation present. when TTL expires it's back to normal. autoscaler-bot: current cluster-autoscaler ignores arbitrary annotations by default; any custom logic must be in an external controller.

Priya: What about race with scale-to-zero? if CA removes all machine sets, pods could be stuck. need fallback.

Maya: +1 on fallback. we should add an eviction-safety-net: if a node is being cordoned and there are pending requests in the NVidia Infer queue, cancel drain for one more cycle and emit alert. low overhead, avoids 503 spikes.

Jordan: ops question — where does the heartbeat come from? per-pod sidecar or node-level daemon?

Aria: node-level daemonset (go binary, very small). it watches /proc for nvml activity and our socket queue lengths, then writes annotation: redwood.warm.heartbeat_ts=<unix_ts>. also increments prometheus metric redwood_node_warm_heartbeat_seconds{node="..."}=now.

Sam: can you paste a sample of the annotation + TTL logic?

Aria: sure:

```
# node annotator pseudo
annotations["redwood.warm.heartbeat_ts"] = now
# drain controller pseudocode
if now - node.annotations.heartbeat_ts < 300: skip_drain("recent-activity")
else: normal_drain()
```

Priya: perf/cost trade: we'll keep nodes idle a bit longer (5m default). how did you choose 5m?

Aria: looked at request inter-arrival for gpu-pinned workloads — median inter-arrival is ~30s, 95th ~4m. 5m captures bursts while not keeping nodes for hours. we can expose as feature-flag per-nodepool.

Maya: region constraints: eu-west spot churn makes TTL risky. suggest adaptive TTL: if spot=true reduce to 90s.

Jordan: also think about warmpool vs heartbeat mixing. we should ensure warm pool autoscaling doesn't fight this. maybe warm-pool nodes get label warmpool=true and our daemon adds heartbeat only to non-warmpool nodes.

Aria: yes, daemon excludes label node.kubernetes.io/warmpool=true. goal is to keep cheaper spot nodes eligible for fast reuse but still reclaimable.

Sam: observability? dashboards + SLO.

Aria: adding metrics:

- redwood_node_warm_heartbeat_last{node="..."} (gauge unix_ts)
- redwood_node_warm_heartbeat_count (counter)
- redwood_node_drain_skipped_total{reason="recent-activity"}

set alert if drain_skipped > 10 in 5m for same ASG -> potential leak.

Priya: experiment rollout plan?

Aria: small A/B: pick two eu-west nodepools (non-warmpool), enable daemon in one, control in other. measure: coldstart rate (first-token latency > 300ms after scale), cost delta, drain_skips, and any evictions failing. 2 week test.

Jordan: can we add a fail-open flag so if annotator crashes CA behaves normally?

Aria: yes it's safe — annotator writes only optional annotations. drain controller must default to normal behavior if annotation missing.

Maya: ops checklist before rollout:
- add prometheus metrics and Grafana panel
- add alert for drain_skipped spike
- schedule canary in eu-west low-traffic cluster
- adaptive TTL toggle for spot pools

Sam: I'll own the Grafana panels. Priya you ok to run the canary test?

Priya: yep, can do next Tuesday. I'll coordinate with infra on IAM needed for daemonset to patch node annotations.

autoscaler-bot: reminder — any external drain controller must be documented in infra runbook and tested against CA's scale-down delays. See runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/cluster-autoscaler-interactions

Aria: thanks all. I'll push a small PR with daemon yaml + basic metrics today. will ping again when PR is ready for review. :rocket:

Jordan: nice. excited to see numbers. :chart_with_upwards_trend:

Sam: thx, keep it minimal. no long lived leases please.

Priya: adding to infra calendar.

Maya: noted — I'll watch for alerts during canary window.

Aria: thread // closing for now, will post PR link soon.
